scenes.heading: Template Lifecycle & Properties (Part 1 of 2)
scenes.narration: Templates. Template Lifecycle & Properties (Part 1 of 2). In this video we review 5 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: What is the general lifecycle a template goes through before it's usable to create pages?
scenes.heading: Create, configure, enable, allow, and publish
scenes.body: A template goes through a clear lifecycle: create it, configure its structure/content/policies, enable it so it's selectable, allow it for specific content branches, and publish it so it's available on the publish environment.

scenes.question: What does enabling a template do?
scenes.heading: It makes the template accessible for selection in the Create Page wizard
scenes.body: Enabling a template makes it accessible for use during the page creation process — this step ensures the template appears as an option when selecting a template for a new page.

scenes.question: What does allowing a template do, and where do you configure it?
scenes.heading: It specifies the content branches or areas where the template can be used, via Page Properties > Advanced > Template Settings
scenes.body: Allowing a template specifies the content branches or areas where the template can be utilized, configured in the root page's Page Properties dialog, Advanced tab, Template Settings section — you can add explicit paths or patterns, e.g. /conf/<folder>/settings/wcm/templates/.*

scenes.question: What happens if the Allowed Templates list is left empty on a page branch?
scenes.heading: The tree is ascended until a value or list is found, so templates allowed at higher levels of the hierarchy are also considered
scenes.body: If the Allowed Templates list is left empty, the tree will be ascended until a value or list is found, meaning templates allowed at higher levels of the hierarchy will also be considered for that branch.

scenes.question: What does publishing a template accomplish?
scenes.heading: It makes the fully configured template, and optionally its content policies, available on the publish environment
scenes.body: Publishing a template is necessary to make the fully configured template available on the publish environment when a page is rendered — you can also select content policies to publish alongside it.
